questions.q: According to this lesson, what makes this capstone worth presenting beyond a basic happy-path demo?
options: Showing the abstention path firing, a real traceable citation, and before/after evaluation scores from a measured tuning change
Using the largest possible embedding model available
Adding as many document sources as possible before the presentation
Skipping the evaluation step to keep the demo shorter
questions.explain: An interviewer has seen plenty of happy-path demos; showing the abstention path, real citations, and measured evaluation improvements demonstrates skills most candidates can't show.

questions.q: What does the 'portfolio sentence' in this lesson emphasize about the finished capstone?
options: That it was built without any evaluation step
That it used the cheapest possible embedding model
That it is a tuned, grounded, cited pipeline with an honest abstention path and a measured evaluation — not just a demo that happened to work
That it retrieves from as many knowledge bases as possible
questions.explain: The portfolio sentence specifically calls out tuning, grounding, citations, abstention, and measured evaluation as the claims worth making — each traceable to a specific lesson.

questions.q: Which chapter does this lesson say became the capstone's actual pipeline build — ingestion through citations and failure handling?
options: Chapter 1 (Why RAG Exists)
Chapter 2 (Embeddings Deep Dive)
Chapter 4 (Building a RAG Pipeline)
Chapter 6 (Capstone) alone, with no connection to earlier chapters
questions.explain: Chapter 4 covered ingestion, retrieval, re-ranking, prompt assembly, citations, and failure handling — the exact stages wired together in the capstone build.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the key difference between this course's RAG pipeline and what the next course, AI Agents, covers?
options: AI Agents removes the need for a vector database entirely
This course's pipeline always retrieves in a fixed shape; AI Agents covers a model deciding for itself when to call a tool, including retrieval
AI Agents does not use the Messages API at all
There is no meaningful difference between the two courses
questions.explain: This course builds a pipeline that always retrieves before generating; AI Agents covers giving the model the choice of when and whether to call tools, building on the agentic RAG pattern from Lesson 25.

questions.q: What course comes next after RAG & Vector Databases in the AI Engineer path?
options: Docker and Deployment for AI Applications
AI Agents
Prompt and Context Engineering
Generative AI and LLMs
questions.explain: AI Agents is the next course in the AI Engineer path's Job-Ready stage, picking up directly from this course's agentic RAG pattern.
